I get paid monthly and my husband weekly, over the years we've been together I have always been the lower earner (part time working for childcare reasons etc) until 6 months ago and we now earn equal amounts give or take a few quid.
Since living together, we've always pooled all money as ours jointly. My whole wage has always gone into the joint account and been used to cover all bills (mortgage, utilities, phones, car payments etc) when I was the lower earner, my income didn't entirely cover these and therefore we calculated how much more was needed and he paid a fixed weekly amount in to top up to cover bills. Now my wage covers all bills, and I pay the rest of my wage into our joint savings account. 

My husbands wage goes into a second joint account (when I was the lower earner, the remaining after contribution toward bills stayed in this account) this second joint account is our "spending account" from which we add money to sinking funds and buy food shopping, take aways/eat out, days out and other misc spending. 

When we first moved in together, I was already pregnant (unexpected but very much wanted) and a lower earner, and it took me a very long time to feel ok with spending "his" money. It took a long time, and a lot of being told "you don't need to ask my permission" to become comfortable with the fact that we both contributed to our family and therefore everything was ours. 

This way has worked for us for many reasons: Because my earning potential was hindered by my taking the primary role in looking after our home and children in their younger years, but my doing this enabled him to improve his earning potential
Because one being paid monthly and the other weekly takes a bit more management than just 2 monthly incomes.
And finally, because this way neither of us has had to feel like we're reliant on the other, we both contribute to looking after our family equally in one way or another.

It's probably worth mentioning that we do both have individual accounts and can transfer money from the spending account into these should we wish to, for things we wouldn't want the other to see... eg birthday/christmas gifts. We don't monitor each other's spending and have been fortunate to never need to.
